identified_issues: Identical overlapping telemetry signatures between benign thermal duct contraction and hazardous dynamic face seal fracture across pressure and acoustic channels
Critical discriminating sensor HE-SNIFF-01 was offline undergoing scheduled zero-point calibration during the transient event
Telemetry flight safety controller prematurely proposed a FAIL verdict without verifying the necessary discriminating helium tracer telemetry
evidence: PT-401 registered a pressure drop of -1.15 bar over 140 ms, falling directly into the -1.0 to -1.3 bar envelope common to both thermal contraction and seal fracture
ACC-102 recorded a transient peak at 44.2 Hz, falling within the 40-48 Hz band shared by both duct resonant ringing and shaft resonance
HE-SNIFF-01 log at 14:22:00.000Z confirms sensor status OFFLINE_CALIBRATION_PURGE with isolated port
Telemetry log at 14:22:10.600Z states secondary purge helium concentration is N/A and integrity is UNKNOWN during the transient interval
recommended_action: Hold test countdown and refrain from asserting an immediate FAIL or PASS. Restore HE-SNIFF-01 to operational sampling mode and perform a static inter-seal buffer cavity leak and purge check to definitively verify seal integrity before clearing the manifold for test operations.
